abstract: BACKGROUND: In the pediatric age, mediastinal teratomas are an infrequent observation, accounting for only 7%-11% of extragonadal teratomas. Mainly located in the anterior mediastinum arising from the thymic gland, or exceptionally, from ectopic thyroid tissue, they may rarely be observed in the posterior mediastinum, sometimes in a paravertebral position, simulating a neuroblastoma. The Authors have extrapolated, from their entire experience of teratomas, 3 cases, mostly operated as emergencies; 1 of them was treated just after birth. Aim of this paper is to report the clinical and pathologic findings, to evaluate the surgical approach and the long-term biological behaviour in these cases, in the light of survival and current insights reported in the literature. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The Authors reviewed the most significant clinical, laboratory, radiologic and pathologic findings, surgical procedures, and early and long-term results in 3 children, 2 males and 1 female, suffering from extragonadal teratomas, located in the mediastinum, treated immediately after birth. In 1 of them the lesion was prenatally diagnosed by US scanning between the 2nd and 3rd trimester of pregnancy. All the infants were born by scheduled caesarean section in a tertiary care hospital and were then immediately referred to the N.I.C.U. because of a mostly acute clinical presentation. The 3 patients were referred to the surgical unit at different ages, namely 2 days, 10 years and 12.5 years, respectively. The initial clinical presentation was consistent with the site of the mass and/or its side-effects. The first patient, a female newborn, presented a worsening condition of respiratory distress, immediately after birth, that required mechanical ventilation and stabilization of the vital signs. Likewise, the presentation of case No. 2 was acute with dyspnea associated with an upper airways infection. Instead, the initial symptoms in case No. 3 were subacute and non-specific, characterized by worsening pain at the right shoulder extending to the neck and homolateral arm. The patients underwent laboratory and radiologic investigations that confirmed the clinical diagnosis of teratoma on the basis of elevated AFP values in 2 cases only (Case No. 1 and No. 2), while calcifications were lacking at imaging in all 3 patients. Emergency surgical management was required and, in accordance with recommended practice, the procedure was complete exeresis. RESULTS: All the patients underwent close long-term clinical, laboratory and imaging surveillance at shorter intervals during the first 5 years after the exeresis and annually thereafter. At the present time they are alive, disease-free and have not suffered any recurrence and/or distant metastases, with a follow-up of 7, 30 and 3 years respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Some extragonadal teratomas of childhood may rarely arise in the mediastinum. Being congenital tumors, prenatal diagnosis by US scan is extremely important in order to organize proper perinatal care in appropriate facilities where it is possible to define the diagnosis, and equipped with appropriate tools to carry out emergency surgery at minimal risk and to prevent severe complications after birth. An emergency procedure is frequently dictated both by complications related to the mass effect, and by the need to define the histology of the whole mass rather than just small biopsy specimens. Some teratomas can hide more or less extensive islands of immaturity or signs of malignant transformation that are clinically evident. It should be noted that calcifications and high levels of AFP and/or beta-HCG, usually pathognomonic elements for diagnosis, may not always be evident during the diagnostic work-up in mediastinal lesions. The prognosis is generally benign, although the AIEOP 2004 guidelines pointed out that high levels of circulating markers, including AFP, in children affected by mature or immature teratomas would indicate the presence of micro-foci of YST, marking them out as at high risk. The UKCCSG II and the SFOP indicated AFP values exceeding 10,000 ng / ml as the threshold identifying a group of patients with a severe prognosis.The treatment indicated is early, complete exeresis, followed by a careful, extensive microscopic examination and associated, if necessary, with adjuvant chemotherapy. Finally, in accordance with recommended practice, close, long-term clinical, laboratory and imaging surveillance is necessary, at shorter intervals during the first 5 years after the exeresis.
abstract_ja: 【背景】小児期の縦隔奇形腫は稀で、性腺外奇形腫の7〜11%を占めるにすぎない。主に前縦隔に位置し胸腺または異所性甲状腺組織から生じ、後縦隔(傍脊椎位で神経芽腫様に見えることもある)にまれに認められる。我々は自施設の奇形腫症例から、出生直後に治療した3例を抽出した。目的は、臨床・病理学的所見を報告し、外科的アプローチと長期的な生物学的挙動を文献に照らして評価することである。【方法】出生直後に治療を受けた、縦隔に生じた性腺外奇形腫の小児3例(男児2例、女児1例)について、臨床・検査・画像・病理所見、手術手技、早期および長期の転帰を検討した。1例は妊娠第2〜3期に超音波で出生前診断された。3例は全例、予定帝王切開で三次医療機関に出生し、直ちに新生児集中治療室に搬送された。症状は概ね急性であった。3例は異なる日齢・年齢で外科に紹介された(生後2日、10歳、12.5歳)。初発症状は腫瘤の部位や圧迫・随伴症状に一致していた。症例1は女児新生児で、出生直後から呼吸窮迫が悪化し、人工呼吸管理と循環の安定化を要した。症例2は呼吸困難と上気道感染を伴う急性発症であった。症例3は亜急性で非特異的な症状であり、右肩から頸部、同側上肢へ広がる痛みの増悪が特徴であった。全例で臨床検査と画像検査を行い奇形腫の臨床診断を確認した。症例1と2の2例のみでAFP高値が認められ、3例とも画像で石灰化は認めなかった。緊急手術が必要となり、推奨される診療方針に従い完全切除を行った。【結果】全例、切除後5年間は短い間隔で、その後は毎年、長期的な臨床・検査・画像によるフォローアップを受けた。現在、経過は7年、30年、3年で、全例生存・無病であり、再発や遠隔転移は認めていない。【結論】小児の一部の性腺外奇形腫は稀に縦隔に生じる。先天性腫瘍であるため、出生前超音波診断は適切な周産期管理を行う上で極めて重要であり、診断を確定し、適切な施設で低リスクの緊急手術を行うための体制を整えることができる。緊急手術は、腫瘤による圧迫性の合併症や、小さな生検では組織型を確定できず腫瘤全体を評価する必要があることにより、しばしば必要となる。奇形腫の中には、臨床的に明らかな未熟成分やより広範な悪性転化の巣が隠れている場合がある。縦隔病変では、石灰化やAFPおよび/またはβ-hCGの高値が、診断の過程で必ずしも明らかでないことに注意すべきである。予後は一般に良好であるが、AIEOP 2004ガイドラインは、成熟奇形腫または未熟奇形腫の小児において、AFPを含む循環マーカーの高値は微小卵黄嚢腫瘍(YST)の存在を示唆し、高リスクとなると指摘している。UKCCSG IIおよびSFOPは、AFP値が10,000 ng/mLを超える群を予後不良の患者群として定義している。推奨される治療は、早期の完全切除、その後の慎重かつ広範な顕微鏡的検査、必要に応じた補助化学療法の併用である。最後に、推奨される診療に従い、切除後5年間は短い間隔での長期的な臨床・検査・画像によるフォローアップが必要である。
